_about: Tables for body/ANATOMY.md: organs (inputs, outputs, dependencies, cascades), tissues, the damage-vs-function rule, timescales, the species profile. Structure is Rex's decision (2026-10-29), numbers placeholders; was proposed (Rex's go-ahead via ChatGPT's notes, 2026-10-29, with its three requirements: organ dependencies and cascades, tissue-level mechanisms, blood composition in CIRCULATION). mark: rex | proposed | open. Tables moved whole to data/library/anatomy.json (no game columns): damage_function, timescales, respiratory.

organs.title: The organs: what each does, needs, gives, and what fails when it fails
organs.source: Standard physiology (Guyton and Hall; Boron and Boulpaep) folded to one function capacity per organ (ANA-ORG). Each organ carries function (0 to 1 today) and damage (0 to 1, lasting; sets the maximum function), per the damage-vs-function rule. Period diseases from MEDICINE.md. Dependencies name the organ whose output is this one's input, so a failure propagates by the cascade column (ChatGPT's requirement 1, outside AI).

tissues.title: Tissues: the structures diseases and deficiencies actually act on (ChatGPT's requirement 2)
tissues.source: Histology folded to functional tissue classes; scurvy as impaired collagen (vitamin C is the cofactor for collagen cross-linking), bone as a calcium and vitamin D store, endothelium as the vessel lining whose damage starts atherosclerosis and whose leak is inflammation. ANA-TIS. Each tissue has integrity (0 to 1) read by the organs built from it.

species.title: The species profile: what changes for a horse, a dog, a fish-person (the reusable engine)
species.source: ChatGPT's point (outside AI), kept: the mechanisms (circulation, respiration, metabolism, repair, signalling) are shared; the anatomy and its parameters vary by species. The profile is a data record, not code. Rex's states of being (BODY.md 6) are species profiles of this kind; the merfolk's form and the fish-person's gills are rows here when the story keeper writes them.
